transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because I feel like I’m always running hot, like I can’t shut the motor off. And lately it’s been causing problems for me at the firehouse, so I figured I needed to talk to somebody about it.
Have you felt unusually energetic, restless, or like your thoughts are racing more than usual?

Yeah, definitely restless. Like during command meetings, sitting still feels almost impossible. My body feels like it’s revving too high, and I’m thinking, I need to get up, walk the bay, check the rigs—just do something instead of being stuck in that chair.
Have you noticed your mood being unusually high, elated, or irritable lately, even if just for a short time?
I don’t think so. I mean, I get irritated sometimes, but I wouldn’t say my mood has been unusually high or elated. It’s more like I’m keyed up, not happy or euphoric.
Have you found yourself talking more quickly or more loudly than usual, to the point where others might notice or comment on it?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think anyone’s told me I’m talking louder or faster than normal. I can get intense when I’m explaining something, but I haven’t noticed it being different lately.
Have you noticed that you need less sleep lately, like you feel rested even if you haven’t slept much?
No, I haven’t really noticed that. If I don’t sleep much, I don’t feel rested—I feel tired like anyone else would.
Have you been doing more activities than usual, like taking on extra tasks or projects, or have you noticed yourself moving around more, like pacing or fidgeting?

Yeah, definitely. I feel like I’m always running hot, like I can’t shut the motor off. I’m always doing something or looking for the next thing to do, and lately that’s been causing problems for me at the firehouse.
Have you found it harder to focus or concentrate lately, like your attention is easily pulled away by things around you?

Yeah, it’s been hard. My attention gets pulled off really easily. Like a radio chirps, or somebody walks past the bay, or I just think about a call from yesterday, and I’m off what I was doing. Then it takes me a long time to get back into it.
Have you had any periods lasting several days or longer where you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?
I don’t think so. I mean, I have bad days like anybody, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had several days where I felt hopeless or stopped caring about things I normally like.
Have you noticed that your speech feels pressured lately, like you can't slow it down even if you wanted to?
I don’t think so. I mean, I talk fast sometimes, especially when I’m worked up, but I haven’t noticed it feeling like I can’t slow it down.
Have you had any nights recently where you slept much less than usual, but still felt like you had plenty of energy the next day?
Not really, no. If I sleep less, I usually feel it the next day. I haven’t had those nights where I’m running on barely any sleep and still full of energy.
Have you noticed that you need significantly less sleep than usual, like feeling fully rested after only a few hours of sleep?
No, I haven’t noticed that. If I only get a few hours, I’m usually tired. I don’t feel fully rested on that little sleep.
Have you had trouble winding down or relaxing, even when there’s nothing urgent going on?

Yeah. That’s actually a big part of why I’m here. I feel like I’m always running hot, like I can’t shut the motor off, even when there’s nothing I need to be doing. And lately it’s been causing problems for me at the firehouse.
Have you noticed that you feel rested even after only a few hours of sleep, even if you don’t feel unusually energetic the next day?
No, I don’t think so. If I only get a few hours, I usually feel worn out or foggy. I wouldn’t say I feel rested from that.
Have you found that you don’t get pleasure or satisfaction out of things that usually make you feel good, like spending time with family, firefighting, or other activities you normally enjoy?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I still enjoy things when I’m actually doing them, I think. I haven’t noticed that everything feels flat or like I can’t get any satisfaction out of it.
Have you ever had a period of time lasting at least two weeks where you felt down or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, or lost interest in most things you usually enjoy?

I don’t think so. I’ve had rough days and stretches where I’m frustrated or worn out, but I can’t think of a two-week period where I was down most of the day nearly every day, or where I stopped caring about most things.
Have you ever had a period of time when you felt down or hopeless every day, or lost interest in things you usually care about, and it lasted for at least two weeks?
No, I don’t think so. Like I said, I’ve had bad days or felt worn down, but I can’t point to a stretch of two weeks where I was down every day or stopped caring about things.
Have you ever gone through a period where you felt like you didn’t need much sleep at all, like you could go for days with very little sleep and still feel completely alert and active?
No, I don’t think I’ve had anything like that. I’ve had nights where I didn’t sleep much, but I wouldn’t say I felt completely fine or extra alert after it.
Have you ever had a time when you felt down or hopeless every day, or stopped caring about things you usually enjoy, and it lasted for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks?

I don’t think so. I know we’ve talked about it a bit, but I can’t remember a time where it was that steady for two weeks—like most of the day, nearly every day. I’ve had bad days, just not that kind of stretch.
Have there been times when, despite feeling down or stressed, your mood would brighten a bit if something good happened, even if just for a little while?

I’m not really sure. I mean, if something good happened, I could probably feel a little better in the moment, but I haven’t really paid close attention to that. It’s not something I’ve noticed as a clear pattern.

The patient continues to endorse symptoms of persistent restlessness, difficulty relaxing, trouble concentrating, and constant motor activation. However, there is no clear evidence of decreased need for sleep, pressured speech, or elevated mood. These findings do not strongly support mania (F30.0) or a primary psychotic disorder (F06.81). The differential still includes ADHD (F90.0), Generalized Anxiety Disorder (F43.0), and possibly a mild depressive episode (F32.0), though no clear anhedonia or sustained low mood. Further clarification is needed to narrow further.

F32.0 (Major Depressive Disorder) and F06.81 (Other specified mental disorder) have been ruled out due to no history of sustained low mood, loss of interest, or anhedonia meeting diagnostic criteria. The focus remains on F90.0 (ADHD) due to symptoms of restlessness, difficulty concentrating, and hyperactivity, and F43.0 (Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety) due to stress-related symptoms impacting functioning at work.
